summary: Tested Roll category form on Materials page. CRITICAL BUG: the Roll 'Specs' branch is NOT rendered — the required inputs material-field-printable_height, material-field-printable_width, material-field-material_type and the roll-stock-hint element are all missing from the isRoll=true render path. As a result the UI cannot compute Material $/ft² (stays $0.00), stock, or waste_per_order for a roll material because printable_height is unreachable via UI. The Cost & Pricing side (roll_cost, roll_qty, machine (ink source), waste_linear_ft) IS present, unit auto-sets to 'roll' correctly, paper-only fields (sheets_per_box) are correctly hidden, roll-printed-cost panel renders with roll-material-sqft / roll-ink-sqft / roll-printed-sqft cells, and the footer note '≈ 4.50 ft²' for waste_linear_ft=1 × 54" width is correct (uses rollWidthIn parsed from Size). Backend curl and roll-materials list endpoint work — the already-persisted '#20 (3641MV52) 3641 Matte Vinyl 52"' shows in /api/roll-materials?module=large-format with price_per_sqft=0.3196 and printable_width=52. Paper regression intact (/api/paper-stocks default '100lb uncoated Cover' unchanged).

ui_bugs.issue: Missing isRoll block in the Specs section. Required inputs printable_width (in), printable_height (in), material_type, and the roll-stock-hint bubble are never rendered when category='roll'. printable_width/material_type only appear if the user separately toggles the 'large-format' module in the module list, and printable_height has NO input anywhere in the file (grep confirms zero occurrences of data-testid="material-field-printable_height" and zero of data-testid="roll-stock-hint").

Because printable_height cannot be entered via UI, rollAreaSqft evaluates to 0 for any UI-created roll → Material/ft² panel shows $0.00 (verified in browser: after entering size=54x50yds, roll_cost=215.72, roll_qty=1, the roll-material-sqft cell displayed '$0.00' instead of $0.32). Save would also persist unit_cost=0 and stock_qty=0 for the material.

action_items: Add an isRoll spec block in Materials.js Specs grid (around line 353, next to isPaper/isSubstrate) with three inputs: material-field-printable_width (form.printable_width), material-field-printable_height (form.printable_height), material-field-material_type (form.material_type). Follow the same styling as the paper block.

Below the Specs grid, when isRoll is true, add a roll-stock-hint bubble mirroring paper-stock-hint. Example content: `Auto: roll width <rollWidthIn>" · area ≈ <rollAreaSqft.toFixed(0)> ft² · stock ≈ <rollStock.toFixed(0)> ft²` using the already-computed rollWidthIn/rollAreaSqft/rollStock variables (they exist at lines 108-115).

Verify that after adding printable_height input, entering 1800 (as per the test spec) with size=54x50yds & roll_cost=215.72 produces roll-material-sqft = $0.32 and roll-stock-hint area/stock ≈ 675 ft².
critical_code_review_comments: Materials.js lines 108-115 compute rollWidthIn/rollAreaSqft/rollMatPerSqft/rollStock but there's no input for form.printable_height in the isRoll UI path → dead computation for UI users. Only direct API POST can trigger correct values (which is how the pre-seeded '#20 3641MV52' material was created).

The Roll-only Specs (printable_width, printable_height, material_type) leak into module-specs for 'large-format'/'stickers' modules — this dual location will cause confusion once the isRoll block is added. Consider hiding printable_width/material_type from the module-specs block when isRoll to avoid duplicate data-testid selectors.
Materials.js is now 551 lines — extraction to MaterialForm.jsx increasingly warranted.
